failures.title: Ferrari F154BH Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: High-Voltage Cooling System Leaks - 2019-Present
items.whatHappens: The F154BH features a complex, multi-circuit cooling system managing both the twin-turbo V8 and the high-voltage battery/electric motors. Plastic coolant fittings and electric water pumps can develop micro-fractures under extreme thermal cycling, leading to coolant loss. If the high-voltage system overheats, the car will enter a severe limp mode or shut down entirely to prevent thermal runaway.
items.repairVsReplace: Standalone pump or hose replacement is feasible (£2,000-£5,000). However, if coolant has contaminated the hybrid inverter or caused internal V8 overheating, a full F154BH engine and hybrid system replacement is often the only viable path. Read our full coolant system failure guide.

items.title: Turbocharger Oil Feed and Seal Degradation - 2019-Present
items.whatHappens: The twin turbochargers are mounted in the hot-vee of the V8. Extreme under-hood temperatures can accelerate the degradation of turbo oil feed lines and internal seals. This manifests as blue smoke on startup, increased oil consumption, or noticeable turbo lag.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo replacement or refurbishment is highly labour-intensive due to the mid-engine packaging, often requiring partial engine removal. If turbo failure has sent debris into the intake or oil system, a full F154BH rebuild is mandatory.

items.title: Hybrid Coupler and Clutch Wear - 2019-Present
items.whatHappens: The F154BH uses a complex clutch system to disconnect the internal combustion engine from the electric motors for EV-only driving. Aggressive track use or frequent aggressive launch control deployments can accelerate wear on these couplers, leading to shuddering during mode transitions or failure to engage EV mode.
items.repairVsReplace: Clutch pack replacement requires splitting the engine from the transmission and hybrid module, making it a major service (£10,000-£20,000). If the wear has damaged the flywheel or motor rotor, a full powertrain replacement is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: As a relatively new architecture (introduced in 2019), long-term failure patterns are still emerging. However, early examples that have received strict adherence to Ferrari's 7-year maintenance program and avoid prolonged track use without proper cooldowns demonstrate fewer thermal-related issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the F154BH
variants.intro: The F154BH is the specific plug-in hybrid variant of Ferrari's F154 3.9L V8 family. It is fundamentally distinct from the non-hybrid F154CB (found in the 488 GTB and F8 Tributo) and the F154CD (Roma, Portofino M). You can confirm your exact engine code by checking the plaque on the engine cover, consulting the vehicle's Ferrari Classiche certification or VIN decoder, or reading the alphanumeric stamping directly on the engine block. Fitting the wrong revision matters critically: the F154BH is physically and electronically integrated with the SF90's 8-speed dual-clutch transmission and high-voltage electric motor assembly. A non-hybrid F154CB will not physically mate to the SF90's hybrid transmission, nor will it communicate with the vehicle's hybrid control unit.

relatives.description: - The non-hybrid 3.9L twin-turbo V8 found in the 488 GTB and F8 Tributo. While it shares the same core V8 block architecture, it lacks the integrated electric motor and high-voltage systems, making it physically and electronically incompatible with the SF90.

- The 4.0L twin-turbo V8 variant used in the Roma and Portofino M. It features a slightly larger displacement and different calibration, and like the F154CB, it is not designed for hybrid integration.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement F154BH - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used F154BH engine for sale can be a viable option only if it comes with a complete, stamped Ferrari service history proving all hybrid system software updates and coolant system inspections have been performed. Given the extreme cost of hybrid component failure, buying used carries a premium risk. Browse vetted used F154BH engine options.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the recommended choice for the F154BH. A proper reconditioning process by a Ferrari-certified specialist will replace the turbochargers, all high-voltage cooling pumps, hybrid clutch packs, and engine seals as standard. This addresses the F154BH's core thermal and hybrid integration weaknesses in one go. Compare reconditioned F154BH options.

items.question: How much does a Ferrari F154BH engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ferrari F154BH engine typically costs between £45,000 and £75,000 for supply only, or £55,000 to £90,000 fully fitted by a certified Ferrari specialist. Used units start around £35,000 but carry a high risk of inherited hybrid integration or cooling faults. Rebuilt units range from £65,000 to £95,000 for a comprehensive strip, rebuild, and hybrid recalibration. Labour typically takes 25-40 hours due to the complex mid-engine packaging and high-voltage isolation procedures.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the F154BH engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues involve the high-voltage cooling system and turbocharger oil feeds. Plastic coolant fittings and electric water pumps can develop micro-fractures under extreme thermal cycling, risking coolant loss into the hybrid inverter. The hot-vee mounted twin turbochargers are susceptible to oil seal degradation, which can lead to oil consumption or turbo lag. Aggressive track use can also accelerate wear on the hybrid clutch packs that disconnect the ICE from the electric motors.

items.question: Which Ferrari models use the F154BH engine?
items.answer: The Ferrari F154BH was developed exclusively for the SF90 Stradale and SF90 Stradale Assetto Fiorano, entering production in 2019. It produces 585 kW (780 PS) from the internal combustion engine, combined with 162 kW (220 PS) from three electric motors, for a total system output of 1,000 PS. It is the sole powertrain option for this specific chassis.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned F154BH engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned F154BH is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the extreme complexity and cost of the hybrid integration components. A proper reconditioning process by a certified specialist will replace the turbochargers, all high-voltage cooling pumps, hybrid clutch packs, and engine seals as standard. Used units rarely come with stamped proof that these expensive preventative updates have been completed, making them a high-risk investment.
